See also: trompetă

Asturian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /tɾomˈpeta/ [t̪ɾõmˈpe.t̪a]
  • Rhymes: -eta
  • Syllabification: trom‧pe‧ta

Noun

[edit]

trompeta f (plural trompetes)

  1. trumpet

Further reading

[edit]
  • “trompeta”, in Diccionariu de la llingua asturiana [Dictionary of the Asturian Language] (in Asturian), 1st edition, Academy of the Asturian Language [Asturian: Academia de la Llingua Asturiana], 2000, →ISBN

Catalan

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From trompa +‎ -eta.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central) [tɾumˈpɛ.tə]
  • IPA(key): (Balearic) [tɾomˈpə.tə]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [tɾomˈpe.ta]
  • Audio (Barcelona):(file)

Noun

[edit]

trompeta f (plural trompetes)

  1. trumpet
  2. trumpeter
  3. (colloquial) bigmouth, blabbermouth
  4. (botany) horn of plenty (Craterellus cornucopioides)
  5. (botany, in the plural) angel's trumpet (Brugmansia arborea)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • trompet
  • trompeta grisa
  • trompeta xinesa
  • trompetada
  • trompetejar
  • trompeter
  • trompetista

Further reading

[edit]
  • “trompeta”, in Diccionari de la llengua catalana [Dictionary of the Catalan Language] (in Catalan), second edition, Institute of Catalan Studies [Catalan: Institut d'Estudis Catalans], April 2007

Galician

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

trompeta f (plural trompetas)

  1. trumpet
  2. trumpeter
    Synonym: trompetista

Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Spanish trompeta[1] or French trompette.[2]

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /tɾõˈpe.tɐ/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /tɾõˈpe.tɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /tɾõˈpe.ta/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /tɾõˈpe.tɐ/

  • Hyphenation: trom‧pe‧ta

Noun

[edit]

trompeta f (plural trompetas)

  1. alternative form of trompete

References

[edit]
  1. ^ “trompeta”, in Dicionário infopédia da Lingua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Porto: Porto Editora, 2003–2026
  2. ^ “trompeta”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

Further reading

[edit]
  • “trompeta”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From trompa +‎ -eta (compare French trompette).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /tɾomˈpeta/ [t̪ɾõmˈpe.t̪a]
  • Rhymes: -eta
  • Syllabification: trom‧pe‧ta

Noun

[edit]

trompeta f (plural trompetas)

  1. trumpet

Derived terms

[edit]
  • atrompetado
  • trompeta de ángel
  • trompeta de la muerte
  • trompeta de los muertos
  • trompeta negra
  • trompetada
  • trompetazo
  • trompetear
  • trompetería
  • trompetero
  • trompetilla
  • trompetista

Noun

[edit]

trompeta m or f by sense (plural trompetas)

  1. trumpeter
    Synonym: trompetista

Further reading

[edit]
  • “trompeta”, in Diccionario de la lengua española [Dictionary of the Spanish Language] (in Spanish), online version 23.8.1, Royal Spanish Academy [Spanish: Real Academia Española], 15 December 2025

Tagalog

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Tagalog) IPA(key): /tɾomˈpeta/ [t̪ɾomˈpɛː.t̪ɐ]
  • Rhymes: -eta
  • Syllabification: trom‧pe‧ta

Noun

[edit]

trompeta (Baybayin spelling ᜆ᜔ᜇᜓᜋ᜔ᜉᜒᜆ)

  1. alternative form of trumpeta
